body.p: Amendments to the Claims: A listing of the entire set of pending claims (including amendments to the claims, if any) is submitted herewith per 37 CFR 1.121. This listing of claims will replace all prior versions, and listings, of claims in the application.
body.br:
1. (Currently amended) vital signs sensor configured to measure or determine vital signs of a user, comprising a photoplethysmographic (PPG) sensor comprising a light source configured to generate light is directed towards a skin of the user, a photo detector unit configured to detect light, wherein light indicative of a reflection of light emitted in or from the skin of the user and a contact surface configured to be placed against a skin of a user, wherein the light from the light source is directed towards the skin of the user via the contact surface, a force measuring unit configured to measure a force applied via the contact surface of the PPG sensor to the skin of the user, and a processing unit configured to extract information regarding a blood volume pulse from an output signal of the PPG sensor during the force applied to the skin of the user and to map the extracted information to a blood pressure value at the force applied to the skin of the user via the contact surface of the PPG sensor.
2. (Currently amended) vital signs sensor claim 1, wherein the optical vital signs sensor is a wrist worn optical vital signs sensor.
3-4 (Cancelled)
5. (Currently amended) vital signs sensor claim 1, further comprising a wristband having a cavity in which a distensible membrane is arranged, wherein the membrane can be inflated or deflated by an air pump unit in order to apply pressure to the PPG sensor.
6. (Currently amended) vital signs sensor claim wherein the force transducer is coupled to the PPG sensor in order to detect force at which the PPG sensor is pressed against a skin of a user.
7. (Currently amended) vital signs sensor claim 1, wherein the force applied to the skin of the user is 15 N.
8. (Currently amended) vital signs sensor claim 1, wherein the blood pressure value is a Mean Arterial Pressure.
9. 10. (Currently amended) of measuring or determining vital signs of a user claim 9, further comprising measuring a blood pressure with an external device, and
calibrating the mapping based on the measured blood pressure.
11. (cancelled)
12. (Currently amended) of measuring or determining vital signs of a user claim 9, wherein only the contact surface of the PPG sensor is used to apply the force to the skin of the user.
13. (Currently amended) A computer program product comprising a computer readable memory storing computer program code for causing the optical vital signs sensor claim 1 to carry out " of measuring or determining vital signs of a user.
14. (Currently amended) vital signs sensor claim 2, wherein the force actuator is configured to apply a force to the skin of the user via the PPG sensor.
15. (New) The optical vital signs sensor of claim 1, comprising a force actuator configured to apply the force to the skin of the user.
16. (New) The optical vital signs sensor of claim 1, comprising a display device that displays the blood pressure value.
17. (New) The method of measuring or determining vital signs of a user of claim 9, wherein a force actuator applies the force to the skin of the user.
18. (New) A non-transitory computer-readable medium that includes a program that, when executed by a processor, causes the processor to:
receive a photoplethysmographic (PPG) signal from a PPG sensor that is in contact with skin of a user and detects a reflection of light emitted in or from the skin of the user, receive a force signal from a force transducer that measures a force applied by a surface of the PPG sensor to the skin of the user, extract pulsatile information regarding a blood volume pulse from an AC component of the PPG signal, determine a blood pressure value based on the pulsatile information and the measured force applied by the surface of the PPG sensor to the skin of the user.
19. (New) The non-transitory computer-readable medium of claim 18, wherein the program causes the processor to control a force actuator to apply the force to the skin of the user.
20. (New) The non-transitory computer-readable medium of claim 19, wherein the program causes the processor to:
control the force actuator to apply a linearly increasing force to the skin of the user, extract a plurality of pulsatile information from the AC component of the PPG signal and a corresponding plurality of measured force, wherein determining the blood pressure value is based on the plurality of pulsatile information and corresponding plurality of measure force.
21. (New)The non-transitory computer-readable medium of claim 19, wherein the medium is included in a wrist-worn device that includes the PPG sensor, the force transducer, and the force actuator.
22. (New) The non-transitory computer-readable medium of claim 18, wherein the force applied to the skin of the user is provided by the user, and the program causes the processor to:
measure the force being applied by the user, and
notifying the user when the force is within a range that is suitable for reliably determining the blood pressure value.
23. (New) The non-transitory computer-readable medium of claim 18, wherein the medium is included in a wrist-worn device that includes the PPG sensor and the force transducer.
